name: SIA Project 25 26
description:
# SIA PROJECT 25-26

In the Municipality of Turin, a system called Participium is being developed — an information system that enables citizen participation in the management of urban environments. It allows citizens to interact with the public administration by reporting inconveniences and malfunctions found in the city (e.g., potholes in the asphalt, sidewalks with architectural barriers, garbage in the streets, broken streetlights, etc.). An example of a similar information system is IRIS in Venice: [https://iris.sad.ve.it/](https://iris.sad.ve.it/?utm_source=gemini). The system, once developed, will be made available as open-source software to all Italian public administrations through the portal [https://developers.italia.it/](https://developers.italia.it/?utm_source=gemini).

A. REPORTS
Citizens can submit reports only if they have registered in the system with a username, first name, and last name. Once the registration is received, the user gets an email with a confirmation link. The registration becomes valid, and the user can use the system only after confirming through that link. Once registered, a citizen can submit reports by selecting a point on the map of Turin (which will be saved with latitude and longitude values) and filling in a problem form with the following mandatory fields: title, textual description, category (chosen from a predefined list). It is also mandatory to attach one or more photos (up to 3 per report, with each photo stored with its file path on the server). The possible problem categories are:
• Waterworks – Drinking water
• Architectural Barriers
• Sewerage
• Public Lighting
• Waste
• Road Signs and Traffic Lights
• Roads and Urban Furniture
• Public Green Areas and Playgrounds
• Other
After entering all the information and the pictures, the system asks the citizen whether they want the report to be anonymous (the name will not appear in the public list of all reports).

B. REPORT LIFECYCLE
Once submitted, the report is in the “Pending Approval” state until the Organization Office of the Municipality of Turin performs a preliminary review of citizen reports, marking them as accepted or rejected. The possible states for a report are: Pending Approval, In Progress, Work in Progress, Suspended, Rejected. After approval, accepted reports move to the “In Progress” state, at which point they are assigned to the technical office responsible, based on the problem category. Once the intervention is planned, the state changes to “Work in Progress”, indicating that the issue resolution has started. In some cases, for organizational or technical reasons, the report can be set to “Suspended”, awaiting further evaluation or resources. When the problem is solved, the technical office updates the status and closes the report. In case of rejection, a written explanation from the Organization Office is mandatory (see next section).
If the intervention must be carried out by maintenance personnel from an external company (for example, Enel X for Public Lighting, or company Y for specific reports based on their content), two cases are possible:

* Case 1: The company has access to Participium. In this case, the technical office assigns the report to users from the corresponding company. External maintenance personnel can move the report from Assigned to In Progress. Staff from the technical office and external maintenance workers can exchange information and comments through the report, but these are not visible to the reporting citizen (nor to other citizens). Once the work is completed, the external maintainer can mark the report as resolved.
Note: Automatic assignment of all reports in a certain category to the external company (bypassing the initial review by the public relations officer of the municipality) is possible only if previously configured by the municipal administrator.
* Case 2: The company does NOT have access to Participium. In this case, the external company updates the technical office outside Participium, and once the problems are solved, a staff member from the technical office will manually move the report to the Resolved state.

C. CITIZEN UPDATES
To strengthen trust between citizens and institutions, the citizen can receive updates regarding their own reports through various channels. First, at every state change, the citizen receives a notification on the platform with the corresponding update. Furthermore, municipal operators updating reports can send the reporting citizen a message through the platform, to which it can reply. The system must allow this functionality to be accessible by external chatbots as well. Each time the citizen receives a notification on the platform, they also get an email (this option can be disabled in the user settings panel, where they can also upload a personal photo).
Moreover, after the approval phase, accepted reports immediately become visible on the Participium portal: they appear both on an interactive map of Turin, geolocated based on the citizen’s selected point, and in a summary table that allows filtering and sorting reports by category, status, or date. In both views, the reporter’s name (“anonymous” if that option was chosen) and the report title are displayed. Clicking on the title opens a page with the description.
Even non-registered users can view both the maps and the summary table. Once logged into Participium, citizens can follow other citizens’ open reports and receive notifications (following the same rules as for their own reports).

D. STATISTICS
The system allows viewing public and private statistics. Public statistics are visible in a dedicated section of the website and concern the number of reports per category, and trends over day, week, or month. They are also visible to non-registered users. In the private section, accessible only to administrators, it is possible to view, in addition to the public statistics, charts and tables.
highLevelGoals: The citizen aims to effectively report various urban inconveniences and malfunctions to the public administration, ensuring their concerns are documented and addressed.
The citizen desires to receive timely and relevant updates regarding the status and progress of their submitted reports, fostering trust and transparency.
The citizen seeks the option to submit reports anonymously, protecting their personal identity while still contributing to urban improvement.
The citizen aims to view and follow other citizens' reports and public statistics to stay informed about community issues and the administration's responses.
The Organization Office Staff aims to efficiently review and categorize incoming citizen reports, making informed decisions to accept or reject them.
The Organization Office Staff seeks to provide clear and mandatory written explanations for rejected reports, ensuring transparency and accountability.
The Technical Office Staff aims to accurately assign approved reports to the appropriate technical offices or external companies based on problem categories.
The Technical Office Staff seeks to effectively manage the lifecycle of reports, updating their status from 'In Progress' to 'Resolved' as interventions proceed.
The Technical Office Staff aims to communicate effectively with reporting citizens by sending messages and updates through the platform, enhancing citizen engagement.
The External Maintenance Personnel aims to update the status of assigned reports to reflect the progress and completion of maintenance work.
The External Maintenance Personnel seeks to exchange information and comments with Technical Office Staff regarding specific reports to facilitate problem resolution.
The Municipal Administrator aims to configure the system to automatically assign reports of specific categories to external companies, streamlining the workflow.
The Municipal Administrator seeks to access private statistics, charts, and tables to gain deeper insights into system performance and report trends.
The Non-registered User aims to view public information such as the interactive map of Turin, summary tables of reports, and public statistics to stay informed about urban issues.
lowLevelGoals: The citizen can create a new account by providing a username, name, and email address.
The citizen can activate their newly registered account by clicking a confirmation link sent to their email address.
The citizen can create a new report by providing a title, geographical coordinates or selecting a location on a map, along with a textual description of the inconvenience.
The citizen can upload one or more photos (up to 3) to supplement the textual description of the urban inconvenience in their report.
The citizen can choose from a predefined list of categories (e.g., 'pothole', 'broken street light', 'graffiti') to classify their report.
The citizen receives real-time notifications on the platform when the status of their submitted report changes (e.g., 'Accepted', 'In Progress', 'Resolved').
The citizen receives email notifications when the status of their submitted report changes (e.g., 'Accepted', 'In Progress', 'Resolved').
The citizen can access a chronological log of all actions and status changes related to their specific report.
The citizen can send a response to messages received from municipal operators regarding their reports.
The citizen can select an option during report creation to hide their personal identity from the public list of all reports.
The citizen can view all publicly available reports displayed as markers on an interactive map of the city.
The citizen can apply filters to the list or map of public reports to view only those matching specific criteria (e.g., 'Resolved' reports, 'Pothole' reports).
The citizen can access charts and graphs displaying aggregated data on report submissions, resolutions, and common categories over time.
The citizen can subscribe to receive notifications about status changes or updates on reports submitted by other citizens, following the same rules as for their own reports.
The citizen can access their user settings panel to turn off email notifications for report updates.
The citizen can access their user settings panel to upload or change their personal profile photo.
The Organization Office Staff can view a list of all newly submitted reports awaiting initial review.
The Organization Office Staff can update the status of a report to 'Accepted' after reviewing its validity.
The Organization Office Staff can update the status of a report to 'Rejected' if it does not meet the criteria for acceptance.
When rejecting a report, the Organization Office Staff must provide a textual explanation for the rejection.
The Technical Office Staff can assign an approved report to a specific internal technical office or an external company from a predefined list.
The Technical Office Staff can update the status of an assigned report to 'In Progress' when planning for work begins.
The Technical Office Staff can update the status of an assigned report to 'Work in Progress' when actual work on the inconvenience starts.
The Technical Office Staff can update the status of an assigned report to 'Suspended' if work is temporarily halted.
The Technical Office Staff can update the status of an assigned report to 'Resolved' upon completion of the intervention.
The Technical Office Staff can compose and send a message directly to the citizen who submitted a specific report.
The External Maintenance Personnel can update the status of a report assigned to them from 'Assigned' to 'In Progress'.
The External Maintenance Personnel can update the status of a report assigned to them to 'Completed' upon finishing the maintenance work.
The External Maintenance Personnel can post textual comments or updates on a report, visible to the Technical Office Staff.
The Municipal Administrator can set up rules to automatically assign reports of certain categories (e.g., 'Road Maintenance') to specific external companies.
The Municipal Administrator can access a dashboard displaying internal statistics on report processing times, staff workload, and other operational metrics.
The Municipal Administrator can define parameters to generate tailored reports focusing on particular aspects of system performance or report data.
The Non-registered User can view a map of Turin with public information displayed.
The Non-registered User can access tables summarizing publicly available report data.
The Non-registered User can view publicly available statistical data and graphical representations of urban issues.
